extraction.name: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB)
extraction.description: A benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks, 58 datasets, and 112 languages, with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB aggregates datasets from multiple existing benchmarks and also creates custom datasets for MTEB using public APIs and available online data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark uses datasets from SemEval, BEIR, Hugging Face datasets, Kaggle competitions, public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, and available Reddit and StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For paragraph-to-paragraph settings, titles and abstracts or titles and posts are concatenated; for arXiv with multiple categories, only the first category is used.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets are grouped into sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph, and sentence-to-paragraph categories; some clustering datasets are framed as both S2S and P2P, and for arXivClustering abstracts are concatenated to titles in P2P.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels come from existing human annotations in source datasets, and for custom clustering datasets labels are generated from human-assigned paper categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For arXiv papers with multiple categories, only the first category is used; clustering splits are created at main-category and secondary-category levels.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark supports versioning at the dataset and software level, welcomes community contributions via pull requests, and provides an automatic submission format for leaderboard additions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased toward tasks with many datasets, and overlap between benchmark datasets and model training data is not controlled for in scores.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include missing very long document datasets, task imbalance with underrepresented summarization and pair classification, limited multilingual coverage for retrieval and clustering, and no code datasets or multimodal benchmarking.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is used for evaluating text embedding models across bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS, and summarization, primarily on test splits and on the MSMARCO dev split.

name.evidence: To solve this problem, we introduce the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB).

description.evidence: MTEB spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages.

url.evidence: MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb .

creator.evidence: Niklas Muennighoff1, Nouamane Tazi1, Loïc Magne1, Nils Reimers2*

publisher.evidence: Datasets and the MTEB leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub2.

inLanguage.evidence: STS12 - STS16 and STSBenchmark are monolingual english benchmarks.

isLiveDataset.evidence: MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb .

rai:dataCollection.evidence: MTEB unifies datasets from different embedding tasks into a common, accessible evaluation framework.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: MTEB incorporates SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside a variety of other datasets from various tasks to provide a holistic performance review of text embedding models.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: These datasets are custom-made for MTEB using the public APIs from arXiv9 and bioRxiv/medRxiv10.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Using national linked electronic health data from hospital admissions and death certification cases of HLH that were diagnosed in England between 1/1/2003 and 31/12/2018 were identified using a previously validated approach.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For S2S datasets, the input text is simply the title of the paper, while for P2P the input text is the concatenation of the title and the abstract.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Several clustering tasks are framed as both S2S and P2P tasks. The former only compare titles, while the latter include both title and content. For ArxivClustering, for example, abstracts are concatenated to the title in the P2P setting.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: For bioRxiv and medRxiv this category is unique, but for arXiv multiple categories can be given to a single paper so we only use the first one.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Through versioning at a dataset and software level, we aim to make it easy to reproduce results in MTEB.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We hope our work makes selecting the right embedding model easier and simplifies future embedding research.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: This means MTEB average scores, which are computed over all datasets, are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While MTEB aims to be a diverse benchmark to provide holistic performance reviews, the benchmark has its limitations.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We evaluate on the test splits of all datasets except for MSMARCO, where the dev split is used following Thakur et al. (2021).
